latest_release.body:
Moves the Docker image to PHP 8.4.27, which fixes two critical PHP vulnerabilities, and makes recurring invoices generate however the scheduler is run. **Upgrade every Docker install**, and update PHP on manual installs.

### Security

- The Docker image ran PHP 8.4.25, which is affected by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution without signing in. The image is now built on serversideup/php v5.0.2 with PHP 8.4.27. Manual installs run the server's own PHP, which has to be updated separately (see the upgrade notes). (#922)

### Fixes

- **Recurring invoices were not generated** unless the scheduler happened to run in the exact minute a schedule was due, in the company's time zone. A crontab that ran less often than every minute, ran late, or was down for a while skipped the period, and nothing caught it up. The scheduler now bills every schedule whose next invoice date has passed, whenever it runs. (#924)
- Saving a recurring invoice counted its next invoice date from the start date, so an edited schedule showed a date in the past. It now counts from today, or from the start date while that is still ahead, in the company's time zone. (#924)
- When a recurring invoice is sent automatically and the email fails, the invoice is kept as a draft to send by hand. (#924)
- An image built from the 2.x source since 8 October did not start, because the serversideup base it builds on moved to v5. The image now pins serversideup v5.0.2 and registers its scheduler where v5 expects it. (#922)

### Upgrade notes

- **Docker:** pull the new image and recreate the container, for example `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. The image runs the scheduler itself, so no cron is needed. `php -v` in the container reports 8.4.27.
- **Manual installs:** update PHP to 8.4.27 or later through your operating system or host. The scheduler needs a crontab entry that runs every minute:

  ```
  * * * * * cd /path/to/invoiceshelf && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1
  ```

  A less frequent entry no longer loses invoices; they are created at the first run after they fall due.
- **Hosts without a crontab** that call `/api/cron` from an external scheduler: set `CRON_JOB_AUTH_TOKEN` in `.env` and send the same value in the `x-authorization-token` header. Since 2.4.3 the endpoint refuses every call without it.
- **Invoices that were missed:** after upgrading, a recurring invoice whose latest period was never billed gets one invoice for it at the next scheduler run, dated that day. Periods missed before that are not billed retroactively; create those by hand. Afterwards, check that each recurring invoice shows the next invoice date you expect.
- If you build the image yourself, rebuild it from the 2.4.7 source. Dockerfiles from earlier 2.x releases no longer start on the current serversideup base.

Docker: `invoiceshelf/invoiceshelf:2.4.7` (also `:2.4`, `:2` and `:latest`).

detail.readme:
Open-source invoicing for people who want to own their business data.

Download InvoiceShelf · Try the live demo · Documentation · Join Discord

> [!WARNING] > The default `3.x` branch is an alpha preview. It is ready for testing and > feedback, but not for production data. Use the supported > [`2.x` release](https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/InvoiceShelf/tree/2.x) for a > production installation. ## Run your invoicing from one place InvoiceShelf is a self-hosted web application for creating invoices, tracking payments and expenses, and keeping customer accounts organised. It is built for freelancers and small businesses that want a focused workflow without giving up control of their data. Want to look around before installing? The [public demo](https://demo.invoiceshelf.com/) includes sample data and resets automatically. - Create invoices and estimates, then export polished PDFs. - Record payments and see what each customer still owes. - Track expenses, taxes, and business reports. - Schedule recurring invoices for repeat work. - Give customers a portal for invoices, estimates, and payment history. - Manage multiple companies and invite team members with scoped roles. - Issue EN 16931 e-invoices: ZUGFeRD / Factur-X PDFs with the e-invoice XML embedded (3.x, with the official E-Invoicing module). Optional official modules can add specialised features without making the core application heavier. ### E-invoicing InvoiceShelf 3.x issues e-invoices to the European standard EN 16931 through the official [E-Invoicing module](https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/module-e-invoicing): - An invoice's PDF becomes a **ZUGFeRD / Factur-X** hybrid e-invoice, a PDF/A-3 file with the EN 16931 XML inside that accounting software reads. This meets the German B2B e-invoicing rules and is one of the formats the French reform accepts. - The XML can also be downloaded on its own, for portals that take a file. - Each invoice shows whether it qualifies and, if not, exactly what is missing. - Tax types carry their EN 16931 tax category and units their UN/ECE unit code. It needs the Gotenberg PDF driver. UBL formats (Peppol BIS Billing, XRechnung UBL) and sending through Peppol are planned. ## Install InvoiceShelf ### Production: InvoiceShelf 2.x Install the current stable release from the [self-hosted download page](https://invoiceshelf.com/download), or run the official Docker image with the `:latest` tag. Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.invoiceshelf.com/installation.html) for the complete setup and upgrade instructions. ### Preview: InvoiceShelf 3.x Use the preview only with disposable or backed-up data: - Download the latest 3.x preview from the [self-hosted download page](https://invoiceshelf.com/download). - For Docker, use `invoiceshelf/invoiceshelf:next` instead of `:latest` in the [official Compose setup](https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/docker). A minimal SQLite Docker setup looks like this: ```bash git clone https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/docker.git invoiceshelf cd invoiceshelf cp docker-compose.sqlite.yml docker-compose.yml # For the 3.x preview, change the image tag in docker-compose.yml to :next. docker compose up -d ``` Open and finish the setup wizard. Read the [Docker guide](https://docs.invoiceshelf.com/install/docker.html) before using InvoiceShelf on a public server. For a traditional web-server installation, see the [manual installation guide](https://docs.invoiceshelf.com/install/manual.html). InvoiceShelf 3.x requires PHP 8.4 or 8.5 and supports MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, and SQLite. Docker includes the required application runtime. ## Learn and get help - [User and installation documentation](https://docs.invoiceshelf.com/) - [API reference](https://api-docs.invoiceshelf.com/) - [Discord community](https://discord.gg/eHXf4zWhsR) - [Bug reports and feature requests](https://github.com/InvoiceShelf/InvoiceShelf/issues) ## Contribute Code contributions are welcome. Start with the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and use the development environment in [`docker/development`](docker/development/README.md). You can also help translate InvoiceShelf on [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/invoiceshelf). ## License InvoiceShelf is released under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3.0](LICENSE).
